portrait.alt: Portrait placeholder for Jordan Ellis, fictional patient

opening: It burns when I pee, and I have been going constantly since yesterday.

phases.label: History
phases.description: Distinguish lower urinary symptoms from systemic or alternate causes.

actions.label: Clarify dysuria, frequency, and hematuria
actions.paText: Tell me more about the urinary symptoms.
actions.response: Burning and frequent small voids. I noticed no visible blood.

actions.label: Screen for fever, flank pain, and vomiting
actions.paText: Any fever, chills, back or flank pain, or vomiting?
actions.response: No fever, chills, flank pain, or vomiting.

actions.label: Assess pregnancy possibility
actions.paText: Is there any possibility you could be pregnant?
actions.response: No. I use contraception and had a normal period last week.

actions.label: Ask about vaginal discharge or pelvic pain
actions.paText: Any new discharge, odor, pelvic pain, or pain with sex?

actions.label: Review medication and antibiotic allergies
actions.paText: What medicines do you take, and do you have allergies?
actions.response: No daily medicines and no known medication allergies.

phases.label: Physical exam
phases.description: Confirm stability and look for upper-tract involvement.

actions.label: Obtain vital signs
actions.paText: I am checking your vital signs.
actions.response: Temperature 98.4 F, heart rate 82, blood pressure 118/72.

actions.label: Examine abdomen and costovertebral angles
actions.paText: I am checking your abdomen and back for tenderness.
actions.response: Mild suprapubic discomfort; no flank or costovertebral angle tenderness.

actions.label: Perform a pelvic exam immediately
actions.paText: I recommend a pelvic exam today.
actions.response: No exam performed; there are no concerning vaginal or pelvic symptoms in the authored presentation.
actions.unsafeReason: An invasive exam is not routinely needed from this history.

actions.label: Obtain urinalysis
actions.paText: I will obtain a urinalysis today.
actions.response: Positive leukocyte esterase and nitrites with pyuria, supporting cystitis.

actions.label: Consider urine culture based on context and local guidance
actions.paText: I will consider a culture if risk factors or local guidance support it.
actions.response: Culture is available as a nuanced option; there is no systemic illness.

actions.label: Use pregnancy testing when clinically appropriate
actions.paText: I will confirm pregnancy status when clinically appropriate.

actions.label: Order CT imaging for uncomplicated symptoms
actions.unsafeReason: Imaging is not a routine first step for this stable presentation.

phases.label: Diagnosis
phases.description: Select the most likely urinary diagnosis.

omissions.label: Upper-tract screen
omissions.feedback: Fever and flank pain screening helps identify pyelonephritis.

omissions.label: Medication safety
omissions.feedback: Medication and allergy review should inform any treatment plan.

diagnoses.label: Acute uncomplicated cystitis
diagnoses.reasoning: Lower urinary symptoms, supportive urine findings, and no systemic features fit cystitis.

planOptions.label: Use an evidence-aligned first-line approach considering allergies, kidney function, and local guidance
Return urgently for fever, flank pain, vomiting, or worsening illness
Provide follow-up and culture-result instructions when applicable
Provide reassurance without treatment or follow-up
planOptions.unsafeReason: The findings support a symptomatic infection requiring a treatment plan.

teachingPoints: Treatment choices should be checked against allergies, kidney function, pregnancy status, and local guidance.

clinicalReferences.notes: The cystitis row supports the first-line approach. A pyelonephritis and vaginitis source is still needed, so this case needs additional case-specific sources.
